literal: Two different are the world's nature: wealth is different, and becoming clear-minded is different.
translation: The way of the world is of two different kinds: acquiring wealth is one thing, and becoming wise and clear-minded is quite another.
modern: உலகத்தின் இயல்பு இரு வேறுபட்ட தன்மைகளைக் கொண்டது; செல்வம் பெறுவது ஒரு வகை, அறிவுத் தெளிவு உடையவர் ஆவது மற்றொரு வகை.
explanation: This couplet explains the dual nature of worldly fortune, which separates material wealth from intellectual clarity. The word 'திரு' refers to wealth or prosperity, while 'தெள்ளியர்' refers to those who possess clear, wise minds. The poet points out that these two qualities do not naturally go together in this world. One may have immense wealth but lack wisdom, or possess great wisdom but remain poor. The repetition of 'வேறு' emphasizes that these two states are governed by entirely different laws of destiny.
